title: The bow that threw kings
hook: kings line up for a bow almost no one can bend, and their crowns hit the floor
carry: ahamkara, the ego, is what falls
tomorrow: why does Karna put down the bow?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Draupadi's swayamvara was announced, and we met the princess who rose from her father's fire: Yajnaseni. Your line: yajna, offer to the fire, and blessing returns.

The arena at Panchala is packed. Kings and princes have come from far and wide, dressed in their best. Brahmins have come to watch. There's music, and the noise of a crowd that has waited for this. Somewhere among the brahmins sit five brothers in borrowed clothes, whom everyone here believes are dead. Then Draupadi enters, carrying a garland, and her brother Dhrishtadyumna rises to announce the terms.
screen: `A PACKED ARENA.` → `FIVE BROTHERS IN DISGUISE.` → `THE TERMS.`

segments.voice: Here's the challenge, in paraphrase. This is the bow, these are the arrows. Up high is a mark, and in front of it a device set in the air, with an opening in it. Whoever strings the bow, shoots through the opening and hits the mark, and is worthy in birth and form and strength, wins my sister. Now a detail the text gives. Drupada had hoped all along to give his daughter to Arjuna, so he had this bow made so stiff that hardly anyone could string it. One by one, the kings try, and the bow beats them. Some can't bend it at all. Some get close, and it springs back and throws them to the ground, their crowns and ornaments scattered across the floor. Great names, humbled in front of everyone. Hindu teachers have a word for what hits the floor with those crowns: ahamkara, the ego, literally the I-maker. It's the part of us that says: I'm the one doing this, I deserve this, everyone is watching me. In the Gita, Krishna says the self confused by ahamkara thinks, I am the doer, when it's nature's forces doing the work. Hinduism doesn't ask you to stop acting. It asks you to act without that swelling I. Many tellers read the swayamvara this way: kings who walked up sure of their own names, thrown down by a bow that didn't care who they were. Tomorrow, someone very different walks up to the bow.
screen: `THE TERMS: STRING, SHOOT, HIT.` · `A STIFF BOW; THE KINGS FALL.` · `AHAMKARA: THE I-MAKER.` · then, large: `ACT WITHOUT THE SWELLING I.`

segments.voice: Fold your hands at your chest, the way Hindus greet each other and the gods with namaste, and bow your head a little. Bring to mind one place where you badly want to be seen as the best: a class, a team, a group chat. With each breath out, set a little of that I down, the way you'd set down a heavy bag. If you pray, offer the work to God and let go of the credit. If you don't, just notice how much lighter the work feels without the crowd watching.
Draupadi's swayamvara. A bow almost no one could bend, a mark beyond a device set high in the air, and kings thrown to the floor.
Your line: ahamkara, the ego, is what falls. Crowns on the floor at Panchala. Day seven hundred forty-one.

chat.meaning: At Draupadi's swayamvara, kings sure of their names were thrown down by the bow. Many Hindus touch elders' feet to set down ahamkara, the ego, and receive a blessing.

tie.story: At Draupadi's swayamvara, proud kings stepped up to Drupada's stiff bow and were thrown to the floor, crowns scattered.

Arjuna.meaning: the third Pandava brother, a great archer

Dhrishtadyumna.meaning: Draupadi's brother, who announces the terms

swayamvara.meaning: a bride's own choosing of a husband

Panchala.meaning: Drupada's kingdom, where the contest is held

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Swayamvara Parva (the arena; Dhrishtadyumna announces the terms; the bow and the mark; the kings fail)
